s.comment: Reported by the original LongMemEval authors. GPT-4o is used as both the answering and judging model, which may inflate scores compared to evaluations using a separate judge.
Baseline reported in the Zep paper as a reference point, not by the original benchmark authors. Judge model not specified separately.
Older-generation memory system evaluated by a competitor (TiMem). Scores reported by others for MemoryBank are consistently low, suggesting it is not well-suited for this benchmark.
Scores for A-MEM vary widely across papers (55–63%), likely due to sensitivity to LLM backbone and judge configuration. Uses GPT-4o backbone here.
Evaluated by a competitor (TiMem) using GPT-4o as backbone. Only this one paper reports MemoryOS results on LongMemEval.
Scores for Mem0 vary widely across papers (49–68%), likely reflecting different LLM backbones, k-retrieval settings, and judge configurations. Uses GPT-4o backbone here.
Self-reported by Zep authors. Uses GPT-4o as backbone. Zep's graph-based memory gives it an advantage on multi-session and knowledge-update questions.
Self-reported by ENGRAM authors. Uses episodic graph-based memory. LLM backbone not clearly specified in the paper.
Evaluated by a competitor (TiMem) using GPT-4o as backbone. MemOS uses an OS-inspired layered memory architecture.
Self-reported by LiCoMemory authors. Uses GPT-4o-mini as backbone, making this one of the few mid-range-backbone results in this score tier.
Self-reported. Uses GPT-4.1-mini (a newer, more capable model than GPT-4o-mini) as backbone — scores may be higher than GPT-4o-mini baselines suggest.
Self-reported by HyMem authors. Combines multiple memory strategies (hybrid). LLM backbone not clearly specified.
Self-reported. Uses Qwen3-32B (open-source) as backbone, which behaves differently from GPT-4o-family models and makes direct comparison harder.
Self-reported by TiMem authors. Uses GPT-4o as backbone and focuses on temporal-aware memory management.
Only reported in the SmartSearch paper. No self-reported or independent evaluation is available for this score.
Self-reported. Uses GPT-4.1-mini backbone (newer than GPT-4o-mini). 'G' denotes the graph-enhanced variant of EMem.
Self-reported by Memora authors. Uses GPT-4.1-mini backbone. Best of two reported configurations.
Self-reported. Index-free variant (slightly stronger than the indexed variant at 87.6%). Uses GPT-4.1-mini backbone.

Evaluated by a competitor (Hindsight/Vectorize). Uses GPT-4o as backbone. Judge: GPT-OSS-120B — differs from GPT-4o used in the original LongMemEval paper and most other entries here, making direct comparison harder.
Evaluated by a competitor (Hindsight/Vectorize). Uses Gemini-3 Pro Preview as backbone — stronger than GPT-4o, inflating score. Judge: GPT-OSS-120B.

Self-reported by Plastic Labs. LongMemEval S split. LLM-as-a-judge with GPT-4o as judge (following the LongMemEval paper's methodology). Uses Claude Haiku 4.5 as backbone. Score on LongMem M (500 questions): 88.8%. Also reported in the Chronos paper (arXiv:2603.16862).
Reported by the Chronos paper, not self-reported. Best of two configurations tested; the GPT-4o configuration achieved 84.8%. The backbone for this configuration is not specified.

Self-reported by Chronos authors. Best of two configurations tested; the GPT-4o configuration achieved 92.6%. This configuration uses Claude Opus 4.6 as backbone, which is considerably more capable than the models used by most other entries here.
